rapidyenc — vendored snapshot
=============================

Upstream:   https://github.com/animetosho/rapidyenc
Commit:     27f435afa0a3a15995001219beca08de29f87a0f (shallow clone, 2026-07-18)
Version:    1.1.1 (RAPIDYENC_VERSION 0x010101 in rapidyenc.h)

The .git directory (and .github/.gitignore) were removed — this is a plain
source snapshot, not a submodule.

License
-------
rapidyenc itself is **Public Domain, or CC0 (or equivalent) where public
domain is not recognised** (stated in README.md "License" section). This is
maximally permissive; no attribution or notice obligations.

Third-party components inside this tree:
- crcutil-1.0/ — Apache License 2.0 (see crcutil-1.0/LICENSE). NOTE: our
  build (crates/nzbkit/build.rs) compiles with YENC_DISABLE_CRCUTIL=1, so
  crcutil is NOT compiled into nzbfast binaries. It is only used by upstream
  as the generic CRC32 fallback on x86; rapidyenc has its own generic
  slice-by-4 fallback when crcutil is disabled. Directory kept for
  completeness / future re-enable.
- The CRC32 folding kernels (src/crc_folding*.cc) derive from zlib-ng
  (zlib license) per upstream README.

Build notes
-----------
Built by crates/nzbkit/build.rs using the `cc` crate (cmake is not installed
on this machine; the cc route replicates the per-file -march flags from
upstream CMakeLists.txt). Encoder is excluded (RAPIDYENC_DISABLE_ENCODE=1 and
encoder_*.cc not compiled) — we only need decode + CRC.

Local patches
-------------
The tree is NO LONGER a pristine snapshot. One defect is patched in place,
in two files, and a re-sync must re-apply it or re-check that upstream has
fixed it:

- src/decoder_neon64.cc and src/decoder_neon.cc, 2 Sep 2026. Both ARM
  decode kernels loaded a whole 16-byte vector (`vld1q_u8` /
  `vld1q_u8_align`) for the 4-byte lookahead past the SIMD region, which
  is all the algorithm consumes and all that `_do_decode_simd`'s
  `lenBuffer` reserves. That is an out-of-bounds read of up to 12 bytes
  past the caller's buffer on every arm64 article decode. It is
  width-aligned and so cannot fault, and it cannot change an answer
  (only lanes 0..3 of the loaded vector are ever read), but
  AddressSanitizer aborts on it - which made `yenc_decode` unfuzzable on
  arm64 the moment ASan started reaching this C++ (e0dedc105). Both
  sites now use `vld1q_lane_u32`, the intrinsic upstream's own comment
  says it looked for. The x86 kernels were already correct
  (src/decoder_sse_base.h loads 4 via `_mm_cvtsi32_si128`).
  Found by the yEnc fuzz campaign; written up in
  research/YENC-NEON-OVERREAD-2026-09-02.md. NOT yet reported upstream.

  The aarch32 half (decoder_neon.cc) is COMPILED AND RUN, just not
  sanitized. No box on this fleet is aarch32, so locally it could only be
  syntax-checked (clang --target=armv7a-none-eabi -fsyntax-only); but
  armv7-unknown-linux-musleabihf is a shipped target (TODO 178, 32-bit
  Raspberry Pi OS) and nightly.yml's `armv7-cross` job builds the
  workspace for it and runs the suite under qemu-user. clang defines
  __ARM_NEON for that triple by default, so this file is live code there,
  not a dead arm. What that job does NOT have is AddressSanitizer, so the
  over-read class stays invisible on aarch32 and this half of the fix
  rests on the argument being identical to the aarch64 one.

- src/crc_folding_256.cc and src/crc_folding.cc, 3 Sep 2026. THE x86 CRC
  TWIN OF THE ENTRY ABOVE, same class and same argument. Both CLMUL
  folding kernels finished a buffer with a full ALIGNED vector load
  (`_mm256_load_si256` / `_mm_load_si128`) while only 1..31 (resp. 1..15)
  bytes remained, reading that many bytes past the caller's buffer. It is
  width-aligned, so it cannot fault - 32 and 16 both divide the page size
  - and partial_fold() masks the surplus out, so the CRC was always
  right. AddressSanitizer reports it as the out-of-bounds read it is:
  the scheduled fuzz smoke's yenc_decode burst died on the vpclmul
  kernel in run 33719528482 (3 Sep 2026), which was the FIRST run to
  reach that kernel - the CRC pin (db85dff50) landed 2 Sep. The
  reproducer is kept at
  crates/nzbkit/fuzz/seeds/yenc_decode/crash-d94c80b4149bae0e461b8c0d86d2f5757efdf9cf.
  Both files now zero-fill and memcpy the tail, which is what the
  `len < 32` / `len < 16` head paths in the same two functions have
  always done - so this makes no new claim about which bytes
  partial_fold ignores, it makes the existing one everywhere. Five sites:
  one in the 256-bit file, four in the 128-bit one (the 48/32/16/0-byte
  tails).

  NOT RUNNABLE ON THIS FLEET, and that is the honest limit on the fix.
  Every box here is arm64, and Rosetta does not implement AVX2 or
  VPCLMULQDQ, so neither patched kernel can execute locally at all; the
  files were compiled for x86-64 with the real flags
  (`clang++ -target x86_64-apple-macos12 -mavx2 -mvpclmulqdq -mpclmul`)
  and verified in CI. The verifying test is
  `yenc_simd::tests::every_reachable_crc_kernel_matches_the_oracle`,
  which sweeps lengths 0..=160 at four alignments and deliberately puts
  each case at the END of its own heap block; it runs on the x86 CI
  runners and pins every kernel that runner can reach. NOT yet reported
  upstream.

Pruned: nothing beyond the .git/.github metadata. The tree is small (~950 KB);
tool/ (CLI + bench sources, not compiled by us) and crcutil-1.0/ were kept.
